reason: A ~25-person Series A fintech is hiring the 'founding member of the Infrastructure & Security team' to own SOC 2 Type II, observability and platform reliability from scratch — the exact regulated-fintech platform/SRE/compliance gap Daniel ran at PayPal and Ripple — while simultaneously hiring four human operations roles alongside an Applied AI engineer.

company.name: Basic Capital
company.one_liner: 401(k)/IRA platform whose 'Retirement Mortgage' finances $4 of investment for every $1 a worker contributes, with recordkeeping, 3(16) administration and alternative-asset access bundled in.
company.stage: Series A — $25M led by Forerunner and Lux Capital, announced 2025-08-18; ~25 employees

evidence_jobs.title: Software Engineer - Infrastructure & DevOps
evidence_jobs.quote: Be a founding member of the Infrastructure & Security team, responsible for the platform reliability, security posture, and compliance readiness that enables Basic Capital to scale with confidence... Own Basic Capital's ongoing SOC 2 Type II compliance, implementing security controls, documenting processes, and working with auditors to achieve and maintain certification

evidence_jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer - Product
evidence_jobs.quote: Architect and ship AI-powered features that enhance the user experience

evidence_jobs.title: Head of Product Development
evidence_jobs.quote: we need to rethink the entire retirement investing stack. Not just the UI. Not just the fees. The actual financial products themselves.

people_spec: Co-Founder & CTO (Anjan Karanam) — owns engineering; the infra/security function reports into him and does not yet exist
Co-Founder & CEO (Abdul Al-Asaad) — owns the burn/margin case for buying platform leadership instead of headcount
Founding Engineer — currently absorbing reliability, compliance and cost work as a side job (no VP Engineering or Head of Infrastructure exists to find; that hire is the open req)
talk_track: I spent the last decade on platform and reliability engineering inside regulated fintech - Ripple, PayPal - where compliance, uptime and cloud spend all land on the same small team. Your Infrastructure & DevOps opening asks for a 'founding member of the Infrastructure & Security team' who will 'own Basic Capital's ongoing SOC 2 Type II compliance,' plus observability built from scratch. Here is the read worth having whether or not you write back: when the first infra hire owns compliance, reliability and cost at the same time, audit evidence eats year one, and the platform work that lets 25 people ship like 60 never starts. The fix is cheap and it happens before the offer goes out - decide which one of those three that person actually owns, and which gets bought or automated instead. At Ripple that same split is what took deploys from hours to minutes and, by my numbers, $8M out of annual run rate. Which of the three would you want them on in month one? - Daniel Kirichanski, Prime Path Global
